gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '8K' and '0.005 mm' labels on these boards are different quantities: Yunzii's own page rates the 'dual 8K' RT75 Pro at 0.1 ms wired but 1 ms on 2.4 GHz (HLPlanet measured 0.65 ms and 1.01 ms), Epomaker's 0.005 mm on the HE75 V2 is the adjustment step with a 0.1 mm shortest actuation point, and the scan rate behind the same 8,000 Hz label runs from 16K (Gamakay NS75) to 128K (Epomaker HE75 V2).
standout_why: Compared against four pages, plus two cited pages that would not load. keebspicks.net (cited) has part of it: it gives the AULA F75 HE as 8,000 Hz wired and 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz and advises 'look at the wireless figure', but it covers none of the Yunzii RT75 Pro, Epomaker HE75 V2, HE80, MCHOSE Jet 75 or Gamakay boards and gives no scan rates. Notebookcheck (cited) has 8 kHz stated against 1,000 Hz tested on wireless, but only for the older HE75 Mag, with no rapid trigger step or latency. HLPlanet's guide (in the results, not cited) says only that a 2.4 GHz dongle 'typically adds 20-100% latency' and has no per-board wired/wireless figures; it lists the RT75 Pro as '1000Hz polling, wired only'. The Tom's Guide and PC Gamer pages (both cited) returned only navigation through the fetch tool, so they were not compared. The measured RT75 Pro pair comes from HLPlanet's separate RT75 Pro review, which was not among ChatGPT's results. None of the pages read puts maker latency per mode, scan rate, and step versus shortest actuation point side by side.
decides: It confirms that '8K' does not separate these boards and it weakens ChatGPT's 'best wireless gaming' case for the Yunzii RT75 Pro: on the dongle its maker's own figure is 1 ms, the interval of a 1,000 Hz board. HLPlanet measured 1.01 ms on 2.4 GHz against 0.65 ms wired, so the cable is the faster mode even on the one board read that claims 8K wireless. For a lowest-latency pick under $100, the stated figures that differ are scan rate (HE75 V2 128K at $76.49, HE80 32K at $59.49, NS75 16K at $63.99) and the rapid trigger step (0.005 mm on HE75 V2 and NS75, 0.02 mm on HE80). The Gamakay NS75 is the lowest-priced tri-mode board read today, but it also carries the lowest stated scan rate, so it honestly wins 'tri-mode with a knob for the least money' rather than 'fastest'. The AULA and MCHOSE rows, and the per-mode figures for the Gamakay boards and the HE75 V2, could not be read today and must be filled before the table is final.

findings.note: Product description read through the store's search API (storecheck): 'delivers an 8K polling rate in both wired and 2.4G modes ... (0.1ms wired/1ms wireless)'. Arithmetic: one 8,000 Hz interval is 1/8000 s = 0.125 ms, so the maker's 1 ms wireless figure equals 8 such intervals, or one interval at 1,000 Hz. The description also states 81 keys and tri-mode (USB-C, 2.4 G, Bluetooth). The full page later returned HTTP 429.
